questions.explain: Query Store is called the flight recorder: enable it on every user database, check the Regressed Queries view daily, and use plan forcing when a bad plan hurts production.
options: Enable it only on weekends
Enable it on every user database and check the Regressed Queries view daily
Only use it for development databases
Disable it to save disk space
questions.q: What does the chapter call Query Store, and what is the daily habit around it?

questions.explain: The rhythm: full backup weekly, differentials daily, log backups every fifteen minutes — with log frequency matching the RPO (15 minutes of acceptable data loss = 15-minute log backups).
options: Full backup weekly, differentials daily, transaction log backups every 15 minutes
Full backup daily only
Log backups weekly
Differentials monthly
questions.q: What is the recommended backup rhythm for production databases?

questions.explain: A backup that has never been tested is not a backup — the chapter requires a quarterly restore drill to non-production, running CHECKDB on the restored copy.
options: Successful nightly backup jobs are sufficient
Run RESTORE VERIFYONLY once a year
Testing is only needed after corruption
Run a full restore drill to a non-production server quarterly and run CHECKDB on the restored copy
questions.q: What is the chapter's minimum standard for verifying backups are actually recoverable?

questions.explain: Queries on a readable secondary run under snapshot isolation semantics, which adds row versioning overhead on the primary — so test the read workload against a secondary first.
options: Secondaries are always perfectly in sync
Queries on a readable secondary run under snapshot isolation semantics, adding row versioning overhead on the primary
Read routing happens automatically
Redo queue growth improves consistency
questions.q: Why should you test a read workload against a readable secondary before relying on it?

questions.explain: The standard tempdb mitigations: configure multiple tempdb data files equal to the number of logical processor cores (up to eight), place tempdb on fast storage, and monitor sys.dm_db_task_space_usage.
options: Increase max degree of parallelism
Disable tempdb autogrowth
Configure tempdb data files equal to the number of logical cores (up to eight) and place tempdb on fast storage
Move tempdb to the C: drive
questions.q: What are the standard mitigations for tempdb contention?
